name: Oath of the Open Road
description: Homebrew — a paladin whose oath is to travelers, wanderers, and the roads that connect them, protecting journeys rather than any single throne or cause.
_notes: Fully homebrew — not official WotC content, and not the same as the third-party 'Oath of the Open Road' published elsewhere (that one uses entirely different feature names). This is the project owner's own oath, for Ferghus, a Paladin of Carix, god of mischief and unexpected consequences. Recovered from git history 2026-08-26 after its mechanical text was accidentally lost during a 2026-04-23 cleanup commit — see the 'Vow of the Open Road' entry in homebrew.json for the full recovery story. Only one Channel Divinity pair is confirmed (3rd level); this subclass may have had additional tenets or higher-level features that were never written down at all, not just lost — worth asking the project owner rather than assuming this is complete.

oath_spells_by_level._notes: These are Ferghus's actual tagged type:'oath' spells (the key was wrongly '1' until 2026-09-08 — every other built-out oath in this project keys by real character level, 3/5/9/13/17, not a 1-indexed tier) — fitting picks for a mischief/chaos deity, but not verified against any 'official' Oath Spells table since none exists for this homebrew oath (all real spells, verified to exist at these levels via live sources; the level pairing itself is thematic choice, not a lookup). 5th-level picks (Enlarge/Reduce, Silence) chosen 2026-09-08 over the character's previous Misty Step/Shatter — project owner deliberately avoided Misty Step here despite it fitting 'open road' thematically, wanting to avoid several party paladins all having teleport. 9th/13th/17th chosen 2026-09-09, project owner's own picks: Incite Greed (3rd-level enchantment, Acquisitions Incorporated) + Galder's Tower (3rd-level conjuration, Lost Laboratory of Kwalish — a wandering paladin conjuring shelter fits 'open road' neatly); Banishment (4th-level abjuration, PHB) + Summon Greater Demon (4th-level conjuration, Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes — the demon can break free of control each turn and turn hostile, which is exactly the 'unexpected consequences' theming Carix calls for); Temporal Shunt (5th-level transmutation, Explorer's Guide to Wildemount — a reaction that displaces an attacker in time) + Steel Wind Strike (5th-level conjuration, XGE).
